ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Read figures (I) and (II), and answer the following questions. <image1> An airplane takes off from place D and intends to fly to an Arab country. The position of D is marked in the figure, located near about the 40° latitude line; combined with the surrounding land-sea distribution, D can be judged to be in the eastern part of the Eurasian continent, near eastern China, around 120°E. Figure (II) is a curve of temperature and precipitation changing with months. To judge the airplane landing location in this question, mainly use Figure (I) and the flight information in the question stem. Then reason: the airplane takes off from D, and its destination is an Arab country, so the flight direction should be roughly westward, toward West Asia or North Africa. The question stem gives that the airplane flies across about 20° of longitude per hour, and flying 1 hour and 30 minutes is 1.5 hours, so it flies across about 20°×1.5=30° of longitude in total. Flying westward 30° from D's location of about 120°E, it reaches near about 90°E, with latitude still roughly near 40°N. Near 90°E and 40°N is in the Xinjiang area of China, and the main airport that it is most likely to contact and land at nearby is Urumqi Airport.

Then, for the airplane to contact the ground, which airport is the most likely one for it to land at?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: Figure (I) is a schematic diagram showing positional relationships with latitude circles, and the note on the figure states “the circles in the figure are latitude lines”. The position of D is marked in the figure, located near about the 40° latitude line; combined with the surrounding land-sea distribution, D can be judged to be in the eastern part of the Eurasian continent, near eastern China, around 120°E. Figure (II) is a curve of temperature and precipitation changing with months. To judge the airplane landing location in this question, mainly use Figure (I) and the flight information in the question stem.

Then reason: the airplane takes off from D, and its destination is an Arab country, so the flight direction should be roughly westward, toward West Asia or North Africa. The question stem gives that the airplane flies across about 20° of longitude per hour, and flying 1 hour and 30 minutes is 1.5 hours, so it flies across about 20°×1.5=30° of longitude in total. Flying westward 30° from D's location of about 120°E, it reaches near about 90°E, with latitude still roughly near 40°N. Near 90°E and 40°N is in the Xinjiang area of China, and the main airport that it is most likely to contact and land at nearby is Urumqi Airport.
